panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is an ECG showing wide-complex tachycardia consistent with RVOT-VT, a finding associated with Double-Chambered Right Ventricle. B: Panel B is a transthoracic echocardiogram (apical 4-chamber view) directly visualizing the anatomical features of Double-Chambered Right Ventricle, including the dividing muscular band and the resulting two chamber appearance. C: Panel C uses Color Doppler to show the hemodynamic consequence of the DCRV anatomy, specifically turbulent blood flow across the muscular band. D: Panel D is a short-axis Color Doppler view demonstrating blood flow across the muscular band (blue asterisk) separating the two RV chambers into the RVOT.

in_text_mentions: A chest radiograph (PA) was sent, and a cardiothoracic index of 0.54 was determined. In order to investigate the patient's condition, a CT coronary angiogram was performed, revealing an obstruction in the right ventricular outflow tract, attributed to subinfundibular hypertrophy (Figure 3) and a perimembranous interventricular communication (Figure 4). Additionally, a coronary catheterization was performed, ruling out significant lesions in the coronary tree, thus suggesting a non-ischemic etiology.
